title: The hearer is told to begin harvesting when captivity is reversed
speaker: the Lord through Hosea
note: Figurative imperative in the oracle (cf. Micah 4:13 Command, Joel 4:13 Study Context); include only if such harvest summonses are recorded.

title: Joel calls drunkards to sober up and weep over lost wine
speaker: the Lord through Joel
recipient: drunkards and all who drink wine to intoxication
note: First summons to lament in Joel 1; the later summonses (1:9, 1:11, 1:13–14) are already recorded.

title: Joel calls the people to lament like a bride in sackcloth
speaker: the Lord through Joel
note: Distinct summons to lament between 1:5 and the priests’ call at 1:9.

title: The Lord ironically bids that Israel’s love of these rites be announced
speaker: the Lord through Amos
recipient: the sons of Israel worshipping at Bethel and Gilgal
note: Ironic imperative exposing Bethel and Gilgal worship; low because it reads more as indictment than direction.

title: Israel is told to prepare to call upon its God
speaker: the Lord through Amos
note: Climactic summons after the refrain ‘you did not turn to Me’ (4:6–11); Amos 4 has no record beyond 4:1.

title: Woe to those who long for the Lord’s day: it is darkness
speaker: Amos, delivering the Lord’s word
recipient: Israelites who desire the Lord’s day
note: Woe warning against presumption, comparable to recorded woes (Amos 6:1–7, Isaiah 5:20–24); 5:19–20 complete the image.

title: The Lord teaches Jonah to share His compassion for Nineveh
speaker: the Lord
note: Closing lesson of the gourd, a teaching question like recorded Zechariah 7:5 and Malachi 1:9; Jonah 4 has no records.

title: The Lord calls His people to remember Balak’s plot and Balaam’s answer
speaker: the Lord through Micah
note: Command to the people within the Lord’s case; ot-micah-v6-1 (6:1–3) covers only the summons to the mountains.

title: The Lord’s voice summons the tribe to hear
speaker: the Lord’s voice through Micah
note: Summons opening the indictment of 6:10–16; similar summonses are sometimes Study Context (Amos 3:1, Micah 3:9).

title: The Lord bids the despisers look and marvel at His unbelievable work
speaker: the Lord, answering Habakkuk
note: Summons to scoffers; Paul quotes it as a warning in Acts 13:40–41, which also has no record.

title: Woe to one who makes his neighbour drunk to see his shame
speaker: the peoples’ taunt within the Lord’s answer
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours
note: Fourth woe of the series; AUD-39-2-6 covers only the first three (2:6–12). Extending that record is the alternative.

title: Zephaniah calls for reverence before the Lord, for His day is near
speaker: the Lord through Zephaniah
note: Same kind of call as Habakkuk 2:20 (ot-habakkuk-v2-20, Command); Zephaniah 1 has no records.

title: The inhabitants of the battered quarter are told to lament
speaker: the Lord through Zephaniah
recipient: inhabitants of the battered place, the traders’ quarter
note: Prophetic summons to wail over the destroyed traders; such summonses are in scope (Joel 1:11 is recorded).

title: The Lord calls the people to consider their ways
speaker: the Lord through Haggai
note: 1:7 repeats the 1:5 call (‘Place your hearts upon your ways’) before the rebuilding order in 1:8.

title: The Lord sends Zerubbabel a message about shaking heaven and earth
speaker: the Lord through Haggai
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: The message runs to 2:23, where the Lord chooses Zerubbabel and makes him like a signet.

title: The Lord calls the dispersed to flee the northern land
speaker: the Lord through Zechariah
recipient: the dispersed, those dwelling in daughter Babylon
note: 2:11 continues the same call (‘Escape safely to Zion’); AUD-42-2-7’s note already treats 2:10–11 as one unit.

title: Daughter Zion is called to rejoice, for the Lord comes to dwell
speaker: the Lord through Zechariah
note: Context line not flagged as a candidate; compare Zechariah 9:9 (ot-zechariah-v9-9), recorded as a Command.

title: Not by might or strength but by My Spirit, says the Lord
speaker: the Lord, through the angel speaking to Zechariah
note: The Lord’s word to Zerubbabel (4:6 is a context line); Zechariah 4 has no records.

title: Do not despise the day of small beginnings
speaker: the Lord through Zechariah
recipient: the returned community rebuilding the temple
note: Teaching rhetorical question (‘who treated the small days with contempt?’), like recorded Zechariah 7:5.

title: Zechariah announces the one called Rising who will build the Lord’s house
speaker: the Lord through Zechariah
note: The message ends with a condition: ‘This will happen if you truly listen to the voice of the Lord your God.’

title: The Lord questions whom the people fasted for
speaker: the Lord through Zechariah
recipient: the land’s people and the priests
note: 7:6 completes the same question: their eating and drinking, like their fasting, was for themselves.

title: The shepherd asks to be paid his wages, if they see fit
speaker: Zechariah, acting as the shepherd
recipient: those who traded in the flock
note: Request that yields the thirty silver pieces; the next direction (11:13) is recorded as ot-zechariah-v11-13.

title: Malachi warns against abandoning the wife of one’s youth
speaker: the Lord through Malachi
note: The charge begins at 2:13–14: offerings are refused because they abandoned the wife of their youth.

title: The Lord sends His messenger to prepare the way before Him
speaker: the Lord Almighty through Malachi
recipient: Israel; the messenger who is sent
note: Source of the messenger saying Jesus quotes (Luke 7:27; Matthew 11:10); link as Additional Scripture.

title: The Lord calls the people to return after straying from His ordinances
speaker: the Lord through Malachi
note: The sentence ‘you, sons of Jacob, do not refrain from the injustices of your fathers’ begins in 3:6.

title: The Lord will send Elijah to turn hearts before His day
speaker: the Lord Almighty through Malachi
note: Promised sending with a charge, like 3:1 (linked via AUD-46-7-24); Luke 1:17 and Matthew 17:10–13 also lack records.

title: John the Baptist calls Judea to repent as the kingdom nears
speaker: John the Baptist
recipient: the people coming to him in the wilderness of Judea
note: Same words as Jesus’ call (K029) but a distinct speaker; origin follows AUD-44-3-7. Luke 3:3 is also unrecorded.

title: A wilderness voice calls for preparing the Lord’s way
speaker: Isaiah’s voice, applied to John
note: Quotation of Isaiah 40:3; Luke 3:4–6 and John 1:19–23 are already linked to this record.

title: Jesus tells John to allow His baptism to fulfil all righteousness
speaker: Jesus
note: Unique to Matthew; John’s attempt to prevent Him (3:14) is the occasion.

title: The devil demands Jesus make bread, leap down and worship him
speaker: the devil (the tempter)
note: Hostile directives, recorded as for wicked rulers; no origin value fits the devil. Luke 4:3–9 demands are also unrecorded.

title: A person does not live on bread alone but on God’s word
speaker: Jesus, quoting Deuteronomy 8:3
note: Luke 4:4 is linked to this Deuteronomy 8 group; Deuteronomy 8:3 itself has no itemized record.

title: Do not put the Lord your God to the test
speaker: Jesus, quoting Deuteronomy 6:16
note: Luke 4:12 is already linked to C0996; add Matthew 4:7.

title: Worship the Lord your God and serve Him alone
speaker: Jesus, quoting Deuteronomy 6:13
note: Luke 4:8 sits on this Deuteronomy 6 group; C0243 (‘Serve the Lord your God’, Exodus 23:25) is an itemized alternative.

title: Jesus commands Satan to go away
speaker: Jesus
note: Jesus’ own dismissal, distinct from the quoted law; Matthew 16:23 // Mark 8:33 (‘Get behind me, Satan’) are also unrecorded.

title: Jesus calls fishermen to follow him
speaker: Jesus
note: Not a listed candidate: the call of James and John (4:21–22) is uncovered. Mark 1:16–20 is also unlinked.

title: You are the salt of the earth; tasteless salt is thrown out
speaker: Jesus
topic: The Little Ones and the Poor
note: Same salt-losing-saltiness saying as Mark 9:50; Luke 14:34–35 is also unlinked. A separate record is the alternative.

title: Let your light shine so others glorify the Father
speaker: Jesus
note: 5:14–15 (light of the world, lamp on the stand) lead directly into the command of 5:16.

title: Reconcile with your brother and settle with your accuser
speaker: Jesus
topic: You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You
note: 5:26 completes the settlement warning; the linked Luke 12:57–59 already includes its parallel (12:59).

title: The eye is the body’s lamp; beware lest your light be darkness
speaker: Jesus
note: Not a listed candidate; found uncovered in a coverage sweep. The Luke 11:34–36 parallel is AUD-46-11-33.

title: Ask, seek, and knock
speaker: Jesus
note: 7:9–11 (the Father gives good things to those who ask) parallel Luke 11:11–13, already linked.

title: Beware of false prophets and recognize them by their fruit
speaker: Jesus
note: Not a listed candidate: 7:17–20 (good and rotten trees) are uncovered and complete the same teaching.

title: Jesus sends the healed man to the priest with the offering
speaker: Jesus
note: Linked Mark 1:40–45 already includes the healing word ‘be cleansed’; the Matthew reference starts only at 8:4.

title: Many will come from east and west; the sons cast out
speaker: Jesus
note: Luke 13:28–29 saying sits in AUD-46-13-22; here it follows praise of the centurion’s faith. His plea (8:8) is a petition.

title: Jesus sends the centurion home: as you believed, let it be
speaker: Jesus
note: The centurion episode (Matthew 8:5–13 // Luke 7:1–10) has no record at all.

title: Jesus orders His disciples to cross to the other side
speaker: Jesus
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported order; Mark 4:35 and Luke 8:22 are also unrecorded.

title: Count the cost: the Son of Man has nowhere to rest
speaker: Jesus
recipient: a scribe offering to follow Him
note: The Luke 9:57–58 parallel is also unrecorded; K038 begins at Luke 9:59.

title: Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead
speaker: Jesus
recipient: a disciple asking first to bury his father
note: Same exchange as Luke 9:59–60, the primary text of K038.

title: Jesus rebukes His disciples’ fear and little faith in the storm
speaker: Jesus
note: The disciples’ cry is a petition; the rebuke (8:26) teaches trust. Mark 4:40 and Luke 8:25 are also unrecorded.

title: Jesus sends the pleading demons out into the herd of pigs
speaker: Jesus
recipient: the demons oppressing two men at Gadara
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Exorcism orders are recorded elsewhere (AUD-46-4-35, AUD-48-16-16); Mark 5:12–13 and Luke 8:32 are unrecorded.

title: The townspeople beg Jesus to leave their territory
speaker: the people of the city
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported request, not a listed candidate; Mark 5:17 and Luke 8:37 are also unrecorded.

title: Jesus tells the paralytic to take courage, for his sins are forgiven
speaker: Jesus
note: ‘Take courage’ sayings are recorded elsewhere (K082); Mark 2:5 and Luke 5:20 lack the imperative and have no record.

title: Rise, take your bed, and go home
speaker: Jesus
note: Same healing order as Luke 5:24; Mark 2:9–11 is also unlinked.

title: Matthew is called to follow Jesus
speaker: Jesus
note: Same call as Levi’s in Luke 5:27–28; Mark 2:14 is also unlinked.

title: Jesus tells his critics to learn why God desires mercy
speaker: Jesus
note: Not a listed candidate: 9:12 (the physician saying) opens the same reply; Mark 2:17 and Luke 5:31–32 are also unrecorded.

title: Jesus tells the healed woman to take courage: her faith saved her
speaker: Jesus
recipient: the woman with the flow of blood
note: Mark 5:34 and Luke 8:48 (‘go in peace’) are also unrecorded; AUD-46-8-50 starts after this healing.

title: Jesus clears the mourners: the girl is not dead but sleeping
speaker: Jesus
recipient: the flute players and crowd at the ruler’s house
note: Same scene as Luke 8:52–54 and Mark 5:39–41, both already in AUD-46-8-50.

title: Jesus sternly charges two healed blind men to tell no one
speaker: Jesus
note: Includes ‘According to your faith, let it happen for you’; secrecy orders are recorded elsewhere (AUD-44-12-15). Their cry is a petition.

title: Jesus sends the Twelve to Israel to proclaim the kingdom and heal
speaker: Jesus
note: 10:1’s grant of authority parallels Luke 9:1–2, already linked; Mark 6:7 is also unlinked.

summary: Minor Prophets gaps are mainly unrecorded summonses (Joel 1:5, 1:8; Amos 4:12; Zephaniah 1:7, 1:11; Micah 6:5) and short references; Matthew 8–9 healing and discipleship words largely lack records or Mark/Luke links.
